summary: A white octagonal concrete light of 1910 on the Saguenay's south shore, with one keeper (1910-1917), automated in 1917 and still flashing at night.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. The walking route starts at a private outfitter's lodge (La Pourvoirie du Cap au Leste).

events.note: First light on an open wooden structure, according to Quebec register 168201. Register 168199 says a first wooden light is said to have been built in 1907. Disputed.
Octagonal reinforced-concrete tower, per Quebec register 168201 and Les amis des phares. LighthouseFriends says 1909.
G. Sergerie, first and only keeper, per LighthouseFriends (1910-1917).
Aga equipment installed; LighthouseFriends says it let the light run without a keeper.
Changed to a white flash every 3.5 s, per LighthouseFriends. The current list gives Fl W 6s.

keepers.name: G. Sergerie
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends prints 'G. Sergerie (1910 - 1917)' and gives the initial only. Marine reports of 1913-1915 list a Sergerie among Quebec keepers, but the OCR columns do not match him to this station by position, so that line is not used.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register 168201, Les amis des phares and the tower's own description give 1910 for the concrete tower. LighthouseFriends gives 1909. Register 168199 says a wooden light stood here from 1907 and was replaced in 1910. The story gives 1910 for the tower and reports 1907 as the register's claim.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved disagreements, shown in the story: range 5 nm (Coast Guard 2025 list, nominal range) against 8 nm (register 168201); focal height 17.0 m (Coast Guard) against 23 m (register); tower height 8.1 m (Coast Guard list, column 7) against 10 m (register 168201, LighthouseFriends, Les amis). Bank: LighthouseFriends puts the cape on the north side of the Saguenay (and the register's municipality is Sainte-Rose-du-Nord); Les amis des phares put the light on the south bank. The story states both and does not choose. First-light year disputed (1907 register 168201; 1907 'is said to have been' in 168199; 1909 LighthouseFriends; 1910 register and Les amis). The 1911 Marine report lists Cape East under 'New Lights' for Quebec (printed p. 71, scan p. 78), which the story now cites in place of the earlier 'list of lights' wording. The keeper G. Sergerie appears only in LighthouseFriends for this light; Marine keepers' tables for 1911 to 1915 print a G. Sergerie, but the OCR columns do not link him to this station by position, so the story does not link him. The Atlantic list's 'Cap à l'Est' is the record's ccg_list_number A1798 entry, not a separate record. No Canadian newspaper search was run; the station has no reported wreck or storm in the sources read, so no storm chapter.
